newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain launches last phase of HK military pullout.
newsitem.headline: Britain launches last phase of HK military pullout.

text.p: Britain on Monday launched the final phase of its military pullout from Hong Kong with the supply and troop ship Sir Percivale sailing in to collect the garrison's belongings before the July 1 takeover by China.
"The ship will take home garrison equipment and belongings in the last stage of our drawdown before the handover," said Major John Herring, a British garrison spokesman.
The Sir Percivale will carry away containers loaded with cargo ranging from live ammunition to a mobile broadcast studio and the garrison's sailing yacht, but no weapons.
The ship docked at Stonecutters Island in Victoria Harbour, where Britain lowered its ensign and shut down its Tamar naval base less than a month ago.
The vessel immediately began loading crates of rifle ammunition that camouflaged trucks brought from an ammunition dump carved into the hill of the former Tamar base.
"It's a bit sad really that we're leaving these people," said Royal Fleet Auxiliary (RFA) second officer Nick Tucker.
"It's a strange situation to be in, coming here to help remove the garrison," Tucker said, recalling earlier RFA missions with Hong Kong Chinese crew.
"These ships used to come here for crew changes when we had Chinese crews. They were well disciplined, they knew their jobs well, we miss them."
The Sir Percivale will be moored alongside the British military warehouse until the final departure on June 30.
Hardware from the garrison's Prince of Wales Barracks on Hong Kong Island and Osborn Barracks on the Kowloon Peninsula will be ferried to the vessel, which can carry 2,000 tonnes.

The ship will sail from Hong Kong to Manila with Hong Kong's three naval patrol vessels -- Peacock, Starling and Plover -- which have been sold to the Philippines. It will arrive in Southampton, England, by late August.
It will not be carrying the 400 or so remaining garrison troops of the Black Watch regiment. They will be flying out.
The military Wessex helicopters that were buzzing around Hong Kong harbour as the ship came in on Monday will also not be in the territory for long. They have been sold to Uruguay.

The Sir Percivale is part of a major deployment by a Royal Navy task force in the Asia-Pacific region this year known as operation "Ocean Wave", said the skipper, Captain Philip Roberts. The 12-vessel force is led by the aircraft carrier Illustrious.

The task force ships will not enter Hong Kong together. One frigate from the group, the Beaver, is docked in Hong Kong this week. Another, the submarine destroyer Chatham, comes in two weeks time as a communications centre for the final moments of British rule, said army press officer Sarah Wood.
After the handover, Hong Kong will become a quasi-autonomous capitalist region of communist-ruled China, and China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) will take over defence responsibilities.
An advance party of 40 PLA soldiers arrived in Hong Kong last month to start getting their new garrison facilities ready.

The Sir Percivale saw action during the 1982 Falklands War, when Britain routed Argentine invasion forces from the south Atlantic colony, and in the 1991 Gulf War when an international coalition drove Iraqi forces from Kuwait.
